title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the preceding pages. X is a surface and S = {x_i}, i in I, a finite set of marked points. For each i, S_i is the circle of tangent directions at x_i, that is (T_{x_i}X − 0)/R_{>0}. Write 𝒮 = ⊔ S_i and let 𝒮̃ = ⊔ S̃_i be the disjoint union of universal coverings, each a line. T_0 ≅ Z is the deck group of a single covering S̃_i → S_i.

A topological group G acts differentiably on (X,S), and therefore continuously on 𝒮. Define G̃ as the set of pairs (u, ũ), where ũ is a continuous lift of u_𝒮 to 𝒮̃. This gives an extension (6): 1 → T_0^I → G̃ → G → 1. G acts on T_0^I by permuting I and through the orientation character, since orientation-reversing maps invert the deck generator.

This page, for X compact:
- The canonical map G → G/G°_{(X,S)} → 𝒯(X,S), where 𝒯 is the Teichmüller modular group (mapping class group, presumably the extended one), is covered by a morphism of extensions (7). Its bottom row is 1 → T_0^I → Sp 𝒯(X,S) → 𝒯(X,S) → 1, and Sp 𝒯 is named the 'special Teichmüller group'.
- In modern terms, Sp 𝒯 is the mapping class group of the surface with tangential base points (unit tangent vectors), equivalently with the punctures replaced by boundary circles fixed pointwise. It is the classical Z^n-extension of the punctured-surface mapping class group, the kernel being generated by the boundary Dehn twists.
- The proof is deferred to pp. 764 ff and 766'.

The NB on this page: if an origin e_i is fixed on each S_i, the universal property of the covering means a lift ũ of u_𝒮 is the same as choosing, for each i, a lift ã_i in S̃_{u(i)} of the point u_𝒮(e_i). This is why the set of lifts is a T_0^I-torsor.

The next page applies the construction to GL(2,R)^{±1} acting on (C,0). There S_0 is the unit circle, and the construction yields the Z-extension of GL(2,R)^{±1} obtained from the universal cover. Restricted to GL(2,Z), this leads toward the extension containing B_3 ≅ the preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R), which is Sp 𝒯 for the once-marked torus.
errors: Injectivity of the left vertical/kernel map T_0^I → Sp𝒯(X,S) and well-definedness of the induced map require that the identity component of Diff(X,S) be suitably simply connected (true in the hyperbolic case where Diff_0 is contractible). In exceptional cases (sphere with ≤2 marked points, torus with 1 point handled separately, disc/plane) boundary twists may become trivial or the identity component contributes; the page does not state these restrictions (the proof is deferred to p. 764 ff).
Minor: G° must act trivially on 𝒯 (it does, being the identity component), but the map G̃ → Sp𝒯 needs G° to lift compatibly; not justified on this page.

ideas.what: Extension of a group acting on a marked surface by Z^I via lifts to universal covers of tangent-direction circles
ideas.modern_name: Framed / tangential-basepoint mapping class group extension; group of lifts to universal cover (analogue of the universal cover of Diff(S^1))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Birman, Dehn-twist theory of surfaces with boundary; folklore)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to tangential base points and to T_{1,1} / SL(2,Z) / B_3 relations; exact construction unsure

ideas.what: Special Teichmüller group Sp𝒯(X,S) as an extension of 𝒯(X,S) by T_0^I
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of the surface with boundary components (boundary fixed pointwise) → punctured mapping class group, kernel generated by boundary Dehn twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Birman exact sequences, Dehn twists); standard in Farb–Margalit
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the Longue Marche (1981) discussion of Teichmüller groups; unsure

ideas.what: Lifts determined by choosing lifts of images of base points (torsor structure)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a uniform 'special Teichmüller group' via a group of lifts G̃ for any differentiable action, with the orientation character twisting the kernel. He then specialises it to GL(2,R)^{±1} and GL(2,Z), i.e. B_3 as the special Teichmüller group of the once-marked torus. This is a documented route by which he built the extended (orientation-reversing included) framed mapping class groups for the Esquisse program. Mathematically it is standard.
missed.quote: Sp 𝒯(X,S) est le groupe de Teichmüller spécial de (X,S)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents the origin of the tangential-basepoint / 'spécial' Teichmüller groups underlying Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard Z^n-extension of the mapping class group by boundary twists, phrased via lifts to universal covers of tangent circles. It is historically interesting terminology ('Teichmüller spécial') but not mathematically new.
